claims.text: A framework integrating detailed chemical-disorder and lattice-distortion descriptors will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity single-phase FCC HEAs more accurately than conventional methods.
High-throughput CALPHAD can be used to screen multicomponent alloy compositions and their phase stability.
Machine learning can augment CALPHAD to predict phonon thermal conductivity in HEAs.
Chemical disorder, mass fluctuations, and lattice distortions can be explicitly represented as predictive descriptors.
High configurational entropy and minimal secondary phases characterize the intended initial FCC HEAs.
Chemical disorder and lattice distortions enhance phonon scattering in HEAs.
Multielement interactions produce lattice distortions relevant to phonon transport.
Disorder-induced lattice distortions scatter phonons more effectively.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces the phonon mean free path.
A reduced phonon mean free path lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
Conventional prediction methods average or overlook disorder effects.
Conventional models underrepresent the effect of compositional disorder on phonon dynamics.
Conventional models typically overestimate thermal conductivity in HEAs.
HEAs selected by the proposed framework will have measured phonon thermal conductivities at least about 20% below values predicted by conventional models.
The framework is primarily applicable to single-phase FCC HEAs with moderate to high chemical complexity.
The framework may be unreliable for multiphase alloys or alloys with substantial microstructural inhomogeneity.
X-ray diffraction can be used to confirm the phase purity and structure of benchmark alloys.
The benchmark will compare measured conductivity rankings and absolute values against predictions from both the proposed and conventional approaches under identical conditions.

The hypothesis is falsified if selected HEAs do not average at least 20% below conventional-model predictions or if measured rankings do not correlate significantly with the proposed model's rankings.
